# import files

Now, we will import the Mothur output files: the shared file (OTU table), the taxonomy file, and the design file (metadata). Make sure these files are in the same directory as this Rmd file, or provide the full path to them.


```{r import-data}
#make phyloseq object
library(phyloseq)
library(microbiome)  # Optional, for further analysis
library(tidyverse)   # For data manipulation

otu_file <- "kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared"
tax_file <- "kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy"
metadata_file <- "kohler.design"

# Read OTU table
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Remove metadata columns
otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]  # removes label, Group, numOtus

# Set rownames as sample IDs
rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group

# Transpose so OTUs are rows
otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

# Create phyloseq OTU table
otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# Check the result
head(otu_tab)
```


```{r}
# --- 1. Read the taxonomy file ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", 
                      sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "")

# --- 2. Extract taxonomy strings and OTU IDs ---
taxonomy_strings <- tax_raw$Taxonomy
names(taxonomy_strings) <- tax_raw$OTU

# --- 3. Split taxonomy strings by ';' and clean ---
taxonomy_clean <- strsplit(taxonomy_strings, ";")

taxonomy_clean <- lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  x <- x[nchar(x) > 0]                # Remove empty strings
  x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)", "", x)       # Remove confidence scores in parentheses
  x <- gsub('\\"', '', x)              # Remove escaped quotes
  trimws(x)                           # Trim whitespace
})

# --- 4. Pad each taxonomy vector to length 7 (Kingdom to Species) ---
max_ranks <- 7
taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  length(x) <- max_ranks  # pad with NAs if needed
  x
}))

# --- 5. Assign column and row names ---
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- names(taxonomy_strings)

# --- 6. Create tax_table object for phyloseq ---
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))

# --- Optional: Check the result ---
head(tax_tab)
```

```{r}
# Load the phyloseq package (necessary for the sample_data function later)
library(phyloseq)

# Read the tab-separated design file
# - sep="\t" ensures tabs are used as the column delimiter
# - skip=1 skips the header line (because header=FALSE is used)
# - stringsAsFactors=FALSE prevents character columns from being converted to factors
metadata <- read.table(
    "kohler.design", 
    header = FALSE, 
    sep = "\t", 
    skip = 1, 
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Rename the columns to match your data structure (3 columns)
colnames(metadata) <- c("SampleID", "SampleType", "Age")

# Set rownames to SampleID (crucial for phyloseq)
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$SampleID

# Remove the redundant SampleID column from the data frame
metadata$SampleID <- NULL

# Create the phyloseq 'sample_data' object
sample_data_obj <- sample_data(metadata)

# The 'sample_data_obj' is now ready to be combined with your OTU table and taxonomy.
```

```{r}
# Combine all components into a single phyloseq object
physeq <- phyloseq(otu_tab, tax_tab, sample_data_obj)
# Check the phyloseq object
physeq
```

```{r}
permanova_result_type <- adonis2(
    bray_curtis_dist ~ SampleType,
    data = as(sample_data(physeq), "data.frame"),
    permutations = 999
)

# Perform PERMANOVA testing the effect of 'Age' on community distance
permanova_result_age <- adonis2(
    bray_curtis_dist ~ Age,
    data = as(sample_data(physeq), "data.frame"),
    permutations = 999
)

# Print results to see the R-squared and p-values
print(permanova_result_type)
print(permanova_result_age)
```
```{r}
bray_curtis_dist <- phyloseq::distance(physeq, method = "bray")

# Perform the PCoA ordination
# 'pcoa_ordination' is the object used for plotting
pcoa_ordination <- ordinate(physeq, method = "PCoA", distance = bray_curtis_dist)

# --- 2. Plot by SampleType ---

pcoa_by_sampletype <- plot_ordination(physeq, pcoa_ordination, color = "SampleType") +
  # Add points with size 3
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # Add 95% confidence ellipses for each SampleType group
  stat_ellipse(geom = "polygon", alpha = 0.2, aes(fill = SampleType)) +
  # Set a clear title
  ggtitle("PCoA of Microbial Communities (Colored by SampleType)") +
  # Use a clean theme
  theme_bw() +
  # Adjust legend to show all SampleType colors clearly
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.5)))

# Save the plot
ggsave("pcoa_by_sampletype.png", pcoa_by_sampletype, width = 7, height = 5, units = "in")

# --- 3. Plot by Age ---

pcoa_by_age <- plot_ordination(physeq, pcoa_ordination, color = "Age") +
  # Add points with size 3
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # Add 95% confidence ellipses for each Age group
  stat_ellipse(geom = "polygon", alpha = 0.2, aes(fill = Age)) +
  # Set a clear title
  ggtitle("PCoA of Microbial Communities (Colored by Age)") +
  # Use a clean theme
  theme_bw() +
  # Adjust legend to show all Age colors clearly
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.5)))

# Save the plot
ggsave("pcoa_by_age.png", pcoa_by_age, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in")
```

```{r}
# Assuming 'physeq' is your complete phyloseq object
# and 'alpha_diversity' contains your richness/diversity metrics.

# 1. Extract the sample metadata into a data frame
sample_metadata <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq))

# 2. Ensure the row names of both data frames match (they should be SampleIDs)
# This step is critical for a correct merge/cbind.
stopifnot(all.equal(rownames(alpha_diversity), rownames(sample_metadata)))

# 3. Combine the alpha diversity metrics with the sample metadata
alpha_data <- cbind(alpha_diversity, sample_metadata)

# --- CRITICAL STEP: Order the Age Factor Levels ---

# Define the logical, chronological order for the Age categories
age_order <- c("Fetus", "Newborn", "7+ days", "15+ days", "20+ days")

# Convert the Age column to a factor with the specified order
alpha_data$Age <- factor(alpha_data$Age, levels = age_order)

# --- Plot Observed Richness by Age (Box Plot) ---
p_observed_age <- ggplot(alpha_data, aes(x = Age, y = Observed, fill = Age)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2), alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Observed Richness by Age", y = "Observed Richness") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Rotate axis labels

print(p_observed_age)

# --- Plot Observed Richness by Age (Violin Plot) ---
p_observed_age_violin <- ggplot(alpha_data, aes(x = Age, y = Observed, fill = Age)) +
  # Add the violin layer to show data density
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.5) +
  # Overlay the boxplot summary (whiskers, median, IQR) without drawing the outliers
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA) +
  # Add all individual data points with jitter
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed Richness by Age",
    y = "Observed Richness"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Rotate axis labels

print(p_observed_age_violin)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries (if not already loaded)
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)

# --- CRITICAL STEP: Join 'Newborn' into 'Sterile' ---

# 1. Get the current sample data as a data frame
sampledf <- data.frame(sample_data(physeq))

# 2. Recode the SampleType factor: Change "Newborn" entries to "Sterile"
# We use 'droplevels' to remove the unused "Newborn" factor level after recoding
sampledf$SampleType <- as.character(sampledf$SampleType)
sampledf$SampleType[sampledf$SampleType == "Newborn"] <- "Sterile"
sampledf$SampleType <- factor(sampledf$SampleType)
sampledf$SampleType <- droplevels(sampledf$SampleType)

# 3. Update the physeq object with the new sample data
sample_data(physeq) <- sampledf

# --- Visualization Steps ---

# Merge rare taxa (optional, but makes the plot cleaner)
physeq_glom <- tax_glom(physeq, taxrank = "Phylum")

# Transform counts to relative abundance for plotting
physeq_rel_abund <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_glom, function(x) x / sum(x) )

# Plot the relative abundance, grouped by the NEW SampleType
p_bar_type <- plot_bar(physeq_rel_abund, fill = "Phylum") +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  # Group bars by the newly recoded SampleType
  facet_wrap(~ SampleType, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) + 
  
  # CHANGE COLOR SCHEME: Use a specific ColorBrewer palette (e.g., 'Set3')
  # You can choose other palettes like 'Dark2', 'Paired', etc.
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") + 
  
  labs(y = "Relative Abundance", title = "Taxonomic Composition (Newborn merged into Sterile)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(), 
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold") # Make facet labels easier to read
  )

print(p_bar_type)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)
library(DESeq2)

# --- 1A. Filtering Rare Taxa ---
# Remove taxa not seen more than 3 times in at least 20% of the samples
physeq_filt <- filter_taxa(physeq, function(x) sum(x > 3) > (0.2 * length(x)), TRUE)

# --- 1B. Rarefaction (for alpha diversity robustness) ---
# Find the minimum library size
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(physeq_filt))

# Rarefy the filtered data to the minimum depth
set.seed(42) # Set seed for reproducibility
physeq_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(physeq_filt, sample.size = min_depth, replace = FALSE)

# Recalculate alpha diversity on the rarefied data
alpha_diversity_rarefied <- estimate_richness(physeq_rarefied, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))

# Re-create the merged data frame for plotting (use the correctly ordered Age factor)
alpha_data_rarefied <- data.frame(
  alpha_diversity_rarefied,
  as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_rarefied))
)

# Order the Age Factor Levels for plotting
age_order <- c("Fetus", "Newborn", "7+ days", "15+ days", "20+ days")
alpha_data_rarefied$Age <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$Age, levels = age_order)

# Visualize Alpha Diversity on Rarefied Data
p_rarefied_alpha <- ggplot(alpha_data_rarefied, aes(x = Age, y = Observed, fill = Age)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Observed Richness by Age (Rarefied Data)", y = "Observed Richness") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p_rarefied_alpha)
```

```{r}
# Calculate the distance matrix on the Rarefied data for consistency
bray_rarefied <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_rarefied, method = "bray")

# Perform PERMDISP for SampleType
dispersion_type <- betadisper(bray_rarefied, sample_data(physeq_rarefied)$SampleType)
print("PERMDISP for SampleType:")
anova(dispersion_type) # Check the p-value: if it's significant (p < 0.05), dispersion differs.

# Perform PERMDISP for Age
dispersion_age <- betadisper(bray_rarefied, sample_data(physeq_rarefied)$Age)
print("PERMDISP for Age:")
anova(dispersion_age)
```

```{r}
#(install.packages("FSA"))
library(FSA)

# Example: Run Kruskal-Wallis first (on Rarefied data)
kw_test_age <- kruskal.test(Shannon ~ Age, data = alpha_data_rarefied)
print("Kruskal-Wallis Test on Shannon by Age:")
print(kw_test_age)

# If kw_test_age$p.value < 0.05, then run Dunn's test:
if (kw_test_age$p.value < 0.05) {
  print("Running Dunn's Post-Hoc Test (p-value significant)...")
  dunn_result <- dunnTest(
    Shannon ~ Age,
    data = alpha_data_rarefied,
    method = "bh" # Benjamini-Hochberg p-value correction
  )
  print(dunn_result)
} else {
  print("Kruskal-Wallis was not significant. Skipping Dunn's test.")
}
```

```{r}
# --- Extract Results (e.g., comparing Muck vs Sterile) ---
# Note: You need to specify the contrast based on your SampleType levels
res <- results(diagdds, contrast = c("SampleType", "Muck", "Sterile"))
res_ordered <- res[order(res$padj), ]

# 1. Convert DESeq2 results to a data frame and filter for significant
res_df <- as.data.frame(res_ordered)
res_df$OTU <- rownames(res_df) # Store the rownames (OTU/ASV ID) as a column
res_df <- res_df[!is.na(res_df$padj) & res_df$padj < 0.05, ] # Filter for significant (padj < 0.05)

# 2. Extract taxonomy for the same OTUs/ASVs
tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(physeq_deseq))
tax_df$OTU <- rownames(tax_df)

# 3. MERGE taxonomy with DESeq2 results based on the shared OTU column
# This is much safer than relying on row order/number with cbind()
res_df_final <- merge(res_df, tax_df, by = "OTU")

# --- Continue with Visualization (if results exist) ---
if (nrow(res_df_final) > 0) {
  # Select the top 15 most significant
  top_res <- head(res_df_final, 15)
  
  # Ensure Genus is a factor ordered by Log2FoldChange for plotting
  top_res$Genus <- factor(top_res$Genus, levels = unique(top_res$Genus[order(top_res$log2FoldChange)]))

  p_deseq <- ggplot(top_res, aes(x = Genus, y = log2FoldChange, fill = log2FoldChange > 0)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = "Top Differentially Abundant Taxa (Muck vs. Sterile)",
      y = expression(Log[2]~"Fold Change"),
      fill = "Enriched in Muck"
    ) +
    theme_bw()

  print(p_deseq)
} else {
  print("No significant differentially abundant taxa found between Muck and Sterile (padj < 0.05).")
}
```

```{r}
#install.packages("indicspecies")
library(indicspecies)

# 1. Prepare data (use the filtered, non-rarefied data for abundance analysis)
OTU_matrix <- as.matrix(otu_table(physeq_filt))
metadata <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_filt))

# 2. Run the IndVal analysis for SampleType
# 'maxcomp = 1' focuses on indicators for single groups (e.g., Muck ONLY)
set.seed(42) 
indval_result_type <- multipatt(
  OTU_matrix, 
  metadata$SampleType, 
  control = how(nperm = 999), 
  func = "r.g", # Calculates IndVal statistic
  max.order = 1 # Only test for single group indicators
)

# 3. View significant results (e.g., p-value < 0.05)
summary(indval_result_type, indval = 0.5, p.val = 0.05)
```
